questions.question: When the card can answer preview questions, how should the preview itself appear on it?

options.label: Inline, expandable
options.description: Each option shows its label and description as now, with the preview collapsed behind a small toggle. The card keeps its current width and rhythm, and nothing jumps when a question has no previews. Longest previews scroll in their own box.
options.preview:
( ) Data layer now, page later        [Recommended]
      Ship the tables and API; no teacher UI yet.
      + show preview

  ( ) Include a minimal teacher list
      One unstyled list behind a flag.
      - hide preview
      +-------------------------------------+
      | game_tiers    T1 | T2 | T3          |
      | games.tier_code  FK -> game_tiers   |
      +-------------------------------------+

  ( ) Full browser now
      Filters, curriculum grid, the lot.

options.label: Side by side, like the terminal
options.description: Options list on the left, the focused option's preview pinned on the right, matching what Claude Code draws. Familiar if you switch between the card and the terminal, but it needs real width and the conversation pane is already narrow.
options.preview:
OPTIONS                |  PREVIEW
  ---------------------- | -------------------------
  (o) Data layer now     |  game_tiers   T1 | T2 | T3
      page later         |  games.tier_code   FK
                         |
  ( ) Minimal list       |  import -> games.json
                         |  deploy -> UPDATE games
  ( ) Full browser now   |
                         |  (preview follows focus)

options.label: Labels only, previews in the terminal
options.description: The card answers the question but never renders the preview; it says a preview exists and offers Open Terminal to read it. Smallest change and no layout risk, but you would be choosing partly blind on exactly the questions that have previews because the detail matters.
